title: How to feel more loved, with Harry Reis, PhD

sentences.en: Feeling loved is something all of us want.
sentences.zh: 被爱是所有人共同的渴望。

sentences.en: It's essential to our health and happiness, but we don't always get to experience it, even in our closest relationships.
sentences.zh: 这对我们的健康和幸福至关重要，但我们并非总能体验到它，哪怕是在最亲密的关系中也是如此。

sentences.en: You probably have people in your life who care about you deeply, your friends, your family,
sentences.zh: 你的人生中可能有一些深爱着你的人，比如你的朋友、家人、

sentences.en: a spouse or a partner, and yet you sometimes still feel unseen or disconnected from them.
sentences.zh: 配偶或伴侣，然而有时你仍然会觉得他们看不见你，或者与他们之间存在隔阂。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: What's the difference between being loved and feeling loved?
sentences.zh: 被爱和感受到被爱之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: How do psychologists define love in the first place?
sentences.zh: 心理学家究竟是如何定义爱的？

sentences.en: Why is feeling loved so essential?
sentences.zh: 为什么感受到被爱如此重要？

sentences.en: And why can it sometimes be so hard to achieve, even when love is there?
sentences.zh: 又为什么有时它会那么难以企及，哪怕爱分明就在那里？是什么在从中作梗？

sentences.en: What gets in the way?
sentences.zh: 是什么在从中作梗？

sentences.en: And what mindsets or habits can help people feel more loved in their everyday lives?
sentences.zh: 哪些心态或习惯能帮助人们在日常生活中感受到更多的爱？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学协会（American Psychological Association）的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Harry Reese, Dean's Professor in the Department of Psychology at the University of Rochester.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是罗切斯特大学（University of Rochester）心理学系院长讲席教授哈里·里斯（Harry Reese）博士。

sentences.en: His research focuses on intimacy and understanding in close relationships, and especially on how being responsive to our partners shapes our relationships.
sentences.zh: 他的研究重点是亲密关系以及亲密关系中的理解，尤其是对伴侣的积极回应如何塑造我们的关系。

sentences.en: Dr. Reese is an APA Fellow and has published more than 250 papers in academic journals.
sentences.zh: 里斯博士是美国心理学协会会士，已在学术期刊上发表了250多篇论文。

sentences.en: He has received Distinguished Career Contribution Awards from the Society for Personality and Social
sentences.zh: 他曾荣获人格与社会心理学协会（Society for Personality and Social

sentences.en: Psychology and the International Association for Relationship Research, and his work has been featured in media outlets, including NPR, The New York Times, and Scientific American.
sentences.zh: Psychology）和国际关系研究协会（International Association for Relationship Research）颁发的杰出职业贡献奖，他的研究成果也曾被NPR、《纽约时报》和《科学美国人》等媒体报道。

sentences.en: His new book, written with happiness researcher Dr. Sonia Leobomirsky, is called How to Feel
sentences.zh: 他与幸福感研究员索尼亚·柳博米尔斯基（Sonia Lyubomirsky）博士合著的新书名为《如何感受

sentences.en: Loved, The Five Mindsets That Get You More of What Matters MoSt.
sentences.zh: 被爱：让你获得更多最重要事物的五种心态》（How to Feel Loved, The Five Mindsets That Get You More of What Matters Most）。

sentences.en: Dr. Reese, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 里斯博士，非常感谢你今天作客我们的节目。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be here today, Kim.
sentences.zh: 很高兴今天来到这里，金。

sentences.en: The title of your book is How to Feel Loved, so let's start there.
sentences.zh: 你的书名叫《如何感受被爱》，那我们就从这里开始吧。

sentences.en: How do you define love in your work, and what's the difference between being loved and feeling loved?
sentences.zh: 你在工作中是如何定义爱的？被爱和感受到被爱又有什么区别？

sentences.en: Well, we take a very broad approach to the word love.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们对“爱”这个词采取了非常广义的理解。

sentences.en: You know, love is one of the most ambiguous words in the English language when you think about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，仔细想想，“爱”是英语中最含糊不清的词汇之一。

sentences.en: It can apply to a romantic relationship.
sentences.zh: 它可以适用于浪漫关系。

sentences.en: It can apply to how parents feel about their children, and it can apply to how you feel about chocolate ice cream.
sentences.zh: 它可以适用于父母对孩子的感情，也可以适用于你对巧克力冰淇淋的喜爱。

sentences.en: So we tried to find a definition that would fit with most kinds of human relationships that people have.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们试图找到一个能够契合人们所拥有的绝大多数人类关系的定义。

sentences.en: And so we defined love in terms of feelings of caring and connection and warmth, the kind of feeling that one gets when one feels understood, cared for, appreciated, and seen.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们从关怀、连结和温暖的感觉来定义爱，也就是当一个人感到被理解、被关爱、被欣赏和被看见时所获得的那种感觉。

sentences.en: So our definition very explicitly goes beyond romance, although romance is certainly covered in that as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的定义非常明确地超越了浪漫关系，尽管浪漫关系当然也包含在其中。

sentences.en: You asked about the difference between being loved and feeling loved, and that's a very important distinction to us and to most people.
sentences.zh: 你刚才问了被爱和感受到被爱之间的区别，对我们和大多数人来说，这是一个非常重要的区分。

sentences.en: Being loved is what other people express and regard with respect to you.
sentences.zh: 被爱是别人对你表达的关怀以及对你的看待和尊重。

sentences.en: Feeling loved is how you feel about what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 感受到被爱则是你对他们所作所为的内心感受。

sentences.en: You know, somebody can love you.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，某个人是可以爱你的。

sentences.en: Somebody can express love to you by giving you presents, by telling you how much they care, by sending you Valentine's Day cards.
sentences.zh: 某人可以通过送你礼物、对你表达关切、给你寄情人节卡片来向你表达爱。

sentences.en: Feeling loved is when you take it in inside, when you feel, yes, that person really gets me, that person really cares about me, that person is really concerned about my well-being.
sentences.zh: 而感受到被爱，是指你将其内化于心，当你觉得“没错，这个人真的懂我，这个人真的很在乎我，这个人真的很关心我的幸福”。

sentences.en: And that's a very, very crucial distinction, because many people are loved, and yet they don't feel loved.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常非常关键的区别，因为许多人都在被爱着，然而他们却并没有感受到被爱。

sentences.en: What does the research tell us about why feeling loved is so important?
sentences.zh: 研究告诉我们，为什么感受到被爱如此重要？

sentences.en: Well, feeling loved is so important because it connects to just a variety of things that are so important for people's lives.
sentences.zh: 嗯，感受到被爱之所以如此重要，是因为它与对人们生活至关重要的各种事物息息相关。

sentences.en: Take, for example, the loneliness epidemic.
sentences.zh: 以孤独流行病为例。

sentences.en: People who are lonely don't feel loved.
sentences.zh: 感到孤独的人就是没有感受到被爱。

sentences.en: On the other hand, people who are not lonely most definitely do feel loved.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，不感到孤独的人则绝对能感受到被爱。

sentences.en: So one way to think about it is at the root cause of a general sense of ill-being and disconnection.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一种思考方式是将其视为整体幸福感缺失和人际隔阂的根本原因。

sentences.en: And that ill-feeling in return is responsible for so many important things in life.
sentences.zh: 而这种不良感受反过来又对生活中的许多重要事情产生影响。

sentences.en: For example, when people don't feel loved, they don't work as effectively.
sentences.zh: 例如，当人们没有感受到被爱时，他们的工作效率就会降低。

sentences.en: Young people in school don't do as well.
sentences.zh: 学校里的年轻人表现也会变差。

sentences.en: And much more interestingly, I think, is the idea that it's not only our mental and emotional health that suffers, but it's also our physical health.
sentences.zh: 我认为更有趣的是，不仅我们的心理和情感健康会受到影响，我们的身体健康也会受损。

sentences.en: It's our proneness to disease.
sentences.zh: 这关系到我们对疾病的易感性。

sentences.en: And interestingly enough, people who don't feel loved tend to die sooner.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，没有感受到被爱的人往往会更早离世。

sentences.en: Are there misconceptions people have about love that make it harder for some of us to actually feel loved?
sentences.zh: 人们对爱是否存在某些误解，从而让我们中的一些人更难真正感受到被爱？

sentences.en: Well, the great irony in all this, I think, is the idea that people often will realize that they don't feel as loved as they want.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这一切中最大的讽刺在于，人们经常会意识到自己没有感受到如自己所愿那么多的爱。

sentences.en: And what they will do is often counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 而他们采取的做法往往适得其反。

sentences.en: That is, it is often the kind of thing that actually makes it harder to feel loved rather than helping them feel loved.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这些做法往往实际上让人们更难感受到被爱，而不是帮助他们感受到被爱。

sentences.en: For example, one of the things that people will do is they try to make themselves as attractive
sentences.zh: 例如，人们会做的一件事就是试图让自己尽可能富有吸引力

sentences.en: as possible, as successful as possible, as strong as possible, as accomplished as possible.
sentences.zh: 尽可能成功，尽可能强大，尽可能优秀。

sentences.en: And if you doubt that people will try this, just take a look at profiles that people post on online dating.
sentences.zh: 如果你怀疑人们会这样做，看看人们在网上约会交友软件上发布的个人资料就知道了。

sentences.en: Those profiles are always trumpeting one's virtues.
sentences.zh: 这些个人资料总是在大肆宣扬一个人的优点。

sentences.en: They never mention one's shortcomings.
sentences.zh: 他们从不提及自己的缺点。

sentences.en: They never mention the things that make one a unique human being.
sentences.zh: 他们从不提及那些让你成为一个独特的人的特质。

sentences.en: And the reason that I say that these strategies are counterproductive is that they may well help you feel admired.
sentences.zh: 我之所以说这些策略适得其反，是因为它们或许确实能帮你赢得赞赏。

sentences.en: It may well make other people think, wow, that person is really impressive.
sentences.zh: 这很可能会让其他人觉得：哇，这个人真的很厉害。

sentences.en: But that's not what feeling loved is about.
sentences.zh: 但感受到被爱并不是为了这个。

sentences.en: Feeling loved is about being recognized and appreciated for the total person that one is.
sentences.zh: 感受到被爱，是作为一个完整的个体被认可和欣赏。

sentences.en: And if you only present a curated image of your strengths and accomplishments, you never allow
sentences.zh: 如果你只呈现一个精心策划的、展示自己优势和成就的形象，你就永远不会让

sentences.en: the other person to see the real you, and you never allow yourself to feel what they might express about the real you.
sentences.zh: 对方看到真实的你，你也永远不会让自己去感受他们对真实的你可能会表达的感受。

sentences.en: So one of the central theses of our book is the idea that in order to feel loved, one has to be able to express the full total self that one has,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们书中的核心论点之一就是：要想感受到被爱，一个人必须能够表达出自己完整、全部的自我，

sentences.en: warts and shortcomings, as well as
sentences.zh: 既包括缺点和不足，

sentences.en: strengths and accomplishments.
sentences.zh: 也包括优势和成就。

sentences.en: Do you run the risk of having everything backfire when you say to somebody, I don't feel like you love me enough?
sentences.zh: 当你对某人说“我觉得你不够爱我”时，会不会冒着一切适得其反的风险？

sentences.en: I mean, what approach do you take in order to get somebody to give you that love and let you feel that you really are appreciated?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为了让别人给予你那种爱，并让你觉得你真的被欣赏了，你会采取什么方法？

sentences.en: I think that question is guaranteed to produce a backlash because, you know, if somebody says that to me, I'm going to get defensive.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个问题注定会遭到强烈的反弹，因为你知道，如果有人对我说这样的话，我会产生防御心理。

sentences.en: I'm going to, well, what do you mean I'm trying to tell you how much I love you, dammit?
sentences.zh: 我会觉得：什么意思？我该死地一直在向你表达我有多爱你，你这是什么意思？

sentences.en: You know, our sense of the way you go about things, if you don't feel as loved as you would
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你觉得没有感受到你希望感受到的那么多爱，我们认为你该采取的方式是

sentences.en: like to feel, is to initiate a series of conversations with another person that allow love to be expressed freely back and forth.
sentences.zh: 与另一个人展开一系列对话，让爱能够在彼此之间自由地表达和交流。

sentences.en: So one of the things that you can do, and this may sound ironic because it starts off with helping the other person feel loved.
sentences.zh: 所以你能做的事情之一——这听起来可能有点讽刺，因为它是从帮助对方感受到被爱开始的。

sentences.en: So we offer a series of mindsets in our book.
sentences.zh: 因此我们在书中提供了一系列的心态。

sentences.en: And the one that I think is the best place to start is one that we call listen to learn.
sentences.zh: 我认为最适合作为开始的那一个，被我们称为“倾听以学习”。

sentences.en: The listen to learn mindset says, when you're talking to another person, really listen to them as if they were going to be a quiz tomorrow.
sentences.zh: “倾听以学习”这种心态的意思是：当你和另一个人交谈时，要真正地倾听他们，就好像明天要进行一场关于此事的随堂测验一样。

sentences.en: So often when we're so-called listening to another person, we're preparing our response to the next, you know, what are we going to say next?
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，当我们所谓的“倾听”另一个人说话时，我们其实是在准备回应接下来的内容，你知道的，我们接下来要说什么？

sentences.en: Where are we going to go?
sentences.zh: 我们要聊到哪里去？

sentences.en: How can I change the topic?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么转移话题？

sentences.en: Oh, how do I get out of this conversation to talk to this other person?
sentences.zh: 哦，我怎么才能结束这段对话去和另一个人讲话呢？

sentences.en: Or how do I impress you with, you know, how I know so much about the thing you're talking about?
sentences.zh: 或者我该如何让你惊叹于我知道多少关于你正在谈论的事情的知识？

sentences.en: All of those things interfere with creating a real meaningful kind of connection.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都会妨碍建立真正有意义的连结。

sentences.en: And if you instead approach the other person with a real genuine curiosity, with a real sense of, I'd really like to know more about that because that's really interesting to me.
sentences.zh: 如果你反其道而行之，带着真正的好奇心去接近对方，带着一种“我真的很想了解更多，因为这对我来说真的很有趣”的心态去交流。

sentences.en: I'd like to know what makes you tick.
sentences.zh: 我想知道是什么驱使着你。

sentences.en: I'd like to know why you feel that way.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你为什么会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: When you went to that movie last night, what was it about that movie that you really liked?
sentences.zh: 当你昨晚去看那部电影时，那部电影里究竟是什么吸引了你？

sentences.en: And something really interesting happens then.
sentences.zh: 这时候就会发生一件非常有趣的事情。

sentences.en: It's almost like a light bulb goes off in the other person's head.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像对方脑海中亮起了一盏灯。

sentences.en: They say, huh, this person's really listening to me.
sentences.zh: 他们会想：咦，这个人真的在听我说话。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's one of the mindsets, the listen to learn mindset, but there are five in the book.
sentences.zh: 好的，这就是其中一种心态，“倾听以学习”心态，但书中一共有五种心态。

sentences.en: So can you talk about the others?
sentences.zh: 所以你能谈谈其他的吗？

sentences.en: What are they?
sentences.zh: 它们是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I actually slipped a second one in there because the listen to learn mindset goes closely with the second mindset that is called radical curiosity.
sentences.zh: 其实我刚刚已经不经意地透露了第二种心态，因为“倾听以学习”心态与第二种被称为“激进好奇心”的心态密切相关。

sentences.en: The idea of being and expressing curiosity about the other person.
sentences.zh: 对另一个人保持并表达好奇心的理念。

sentences.en: You know, people are so interesting.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人是如此有趣。

sentences.en: You know, we psychologists are perennially interested in what makes people tick, what drives their behavior.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们心理学家一直对是什么驱使人们、是什么驱动他们的行为充满兴趣。

sentences.en: So when you show enthusiasm, when you show energy, when you show that you're really and genuinely interested in the other person, that's what ticks off the process.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你表现出热情、表现出活力、表现出你对另一个人真的有且只有纯粹的兴趣时，这就是开启整个过程的钥匙。

sentences.en: Now, close to that is a third mindset, which we call the open heart mindset, which essentially
sentences.zh: 与此紧密相关的是第三种心态，我们称之为“敞开心扉”的心态，它的核心实质

sentences.en: has the idea that when one shows interest in another person, it can't just be, you know,
sentences.zh: 在于，当一个人对另一个人表现出兴趣时，不能仅仅停留在

sentences.en: I'm taking notes for the test tomorrow.
sentences.zh: “我在为明天的考试做笔记”这种层面。

sentences.en: It's got to be accompanied by a sense of caring and concern, a sense of compassion for the other person, a sense that you're really interested in their well-being.
sentences.zh: 它必须伴随着一种关怀和关注、对另一个人的同情心，以及一种你真的关心他们幸福的感觉。

sentences.en: You really want to express positive, benevolent feelings toward them.
sentences.zh: 你真的想向他们表达积极的、仁慈的情感。

sentences.en: Some listeners may be thinking, but wait a minute, what he's talking about is going to help the other person feel loved.
sentences.zh: 有些听众可能会想：但是等等，他所说的这些明明是在帮助另一个人感受到被爱。

sentences.en: How does that make me feel more loved?
sentences.zh: 这怎么能让我感觉自己获得更多的爱呢？

sentences.en: And the answer lies in a process that's very well known to researchers who study social interaction.
sentences.zh: 答案在于一个研究社会互动的研究人员非常熟悉的机制。

sentences.en: The idea that reciprocity is one of the strongest rules of social behavior that we have.
sentences.zh: 这就是：互惠原则是我们所拥有的社会行为中最强有力的规则之一。

sentences.en: So think, let's say you do the three mindsets that I was just talking about.
sentences.zh: 所以想想看，假设你实践了我刚才谈到的那三种心态。

sentences.en: Well, that will lift the other person up, much like on a seesaw when you go down and you help the other person rise up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那将会提升另一个人，就像坐在跷跷板上一样，当你往下坐时，你帮助另一个人升了起来。

sentences.en: And then what happens?
sentences.zh: 然后会发生什么？

sentences.en: They return the favor.
sentences.zh: 他们会投桃报李。

sentences.en: And it's the returning the favor that gives you an opportunity to express the fourth mindset.
sentences.zh: 正是这种投桃报李为你提供了一个表达第四种心态的机会。

sentences.en: And the fourth mindset is about being open and sharing and vulnerable about oneself.
sentences.zh: 第四种心态是关于对自我保持开放、分享和脆弱。

sentences.en: So disclosing things that are real about oneself, not just talking about superficial attitudes,
sentences.zh: 因此，要坦白关于自己的真实事情，而不仅仅是谈论表面的态度，

sentences.en: not just talking about the weather, not just trumpeting one's strengths, but instead getting
sentences.zh: 不只是谈论天气，不只是大肆宣扬自己的优点，而是要达到这样一个地步：

sentences.en: to a point where one can share what makes one a unique human being, what's special, what's interesting.
sentences.zh: 一个人能够分享是什么让自己成为了一个独特的人，是什么让自己如此特别和有趣。

sentences.en: And when the other person responds positively to that, that's when you kick off the back and forth dynamic of sharing and listening and sharing and showing appreciation.
sentences.zh: 而当对方对此做出积极回应时，你就开启了分享、倾听、再分享并表达感激的这种来来往往的动态循环。

sentences.en: And it goes back and forth.
sentences.zh: 并且这种循环会持续下去。

sentences.en: And as a result of those kinds of conversations, a person is likely to feel loved.
sentences.zh: 而作为这类对话的结果，这个人更有可能会感受到被爱。

sentences.en: I'm going to play devil's advocate for a minute here.
sentences.zh: 在这里我先扮演一下唱反调的角色。

sentences.en: You say in the book that the key to feeling more loved is not to change yourself, but then you offer some strategies that actually might ask some people to be different, to listen
sentences.zh: 你在书中提到，感受到更多爱的关键不在于改变自己，但随后你又提出了一些策略，这些策略实际上可能会要求某些人做出改变——去更好地倾听、

sentences.en: better, to ask more questions, to be more interested in the other person.
sentences.zh: 提出更多问题、对另一个人表现出更多的兴趣。

sentences.en: I mean, for some people, that could be a pretty fundamental change.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对某些人来说，这可能是一个相当根本的改变。

sentences.en: Some folks, as you said, they're not good listeners.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，有些人并不擅长倾听。

sentences.en: They're just waiting for the opportunity to say what it is that they want to say.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在等待机会说出自己想说的话。

sentences.en: So how do you respond to that?
sentences.zh: 那你对这种说法有什么回应呢？

sentences.en: Don't you have to change in some way?
sentences.zh: 难道你不需要在某些方面做出改变吗？

sentences.en: I love that question.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这个问题。

sentences.en: And what I would say is we're suggesting that you don't change yourself, but that you change your behavior.
sentences.zh: 我的回答是：我们建议你不要改变自己，而是要改变你的行为。

sentences.en: It's not saying you need to be more attractive.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说你需要变得更有吸引力。

sentences.en: You need to publish more articles.
sentences.zh: 你不需要发表更多的文章。

sentences.en: You need to go to the gym more often.
sentences.zh: 你不需要更频繁地去健身房。

sentences.en: We're not saying you need to change who you are.
sentences.zh: 我们并不是说你需要改变你是谁。

sentences.en: We're saying you need to change the way you interact with other people.
sentences.zh: 我们是说你需要改变你与他人互动的方式。

sentences.en: You know, for some people, some of these behaviors may seem a little foreign.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，对某些人来说，其中一些行为可能会显得有点陌生。

sentences.en: So one way to think about it is as an experiment.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一种思考方式是把它当作一场实验。

sentences.en: Try doing something different.
sentences.zh: 尝试做一些不同的事情。

sentences.en: When you're talking to someone tonight and they tell you about something that happened to them, say, tell me more.
sentences.zh: 今天晚上当你和某人谈话，而他们向你讲述发生在他们身上的事情时，说一句：告诉我更多。

sentences.en: I'd really like to know more about what that meal felt like.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想多了解一下那顿饭的感觉。

sentences.en: What, which of the foods did you really like the best?
sentences.zh: 哪样食物你最喜欢？

sentences.en: And experiment with that.
sentences.zh: 去尝试这个实验。

sentences.en: That doesn't require changing your personality.
sentences.zh: 这不需要改变你的个性。

sentences.en: It doesn't require changing who you fundamentally are as a person.
sentences.zh: 它不需要改变你作为一个人的根本本质。

sentences.en: It simply means adopting a different orientation, a different approach when you're talking to somebody.
sentences.zh: 它仅仅意味着在与人交谈时，采取一种不同的方向，一种不同的方法。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break.
sentences.zh: 我们要稍作休息。

sentences.en: When we return, I'll talk more with Dr. Reese about how to get these conversations started.
sentences.zh: 休息回来后，我将与里斯博士继续探讨如何开启这些对话。

sentences.en: So if you've identified a relationship in your life where you think you'd like to feel more loved, how do you start?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你已经在生活中确定了一段你希望能感受到更多爱的关系，你该如何开始呢？

sentences.en: What do you do first?
sentences.zh: 你首先要做什么？

sentences.en: In principle, you can start with any of the mindsets.
sentences.zh: 原则上，你可以从任何一种思维模式开始。

sentences.en: The one that I like to start with when I'm trying to create these kinds of feelings is the listen to learn one.
sentences.zh: 当我试图营造这种感觉时，我最喜欢从“倾听以学习”这种模式开始。

sentences.en: It's the one I think that's most controllable.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是最容易控制的一种。

sentences.en: You can simply walk into the next conversation and start to ask the person questions about what they're saying.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接进入下一场对话，开始向对方询问他们所谈论的内容。

sentences.en: Don't try to get in, you know, your strengths and your accomplishments.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，不要急于展示你的优势和成就。

sentences.en: Simply talk more about what the other person's interested in.
sentences.zh: 只需多谈谈对方感兴趣的话题。

sentences.en: Now, interestingly enough, this is not entirely a new suggestion.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这并非一个完全崭新的建议。

sentences.en: In 1938, Dale Carnegie wrote the second bestselling book of all time, How to Win Friends and Influence
sentences.zh: 1938年，戴尔·卡耐基写下了有史以来第二畅销的书籍《如何赢得朋友并影响》

sentences.en: People.
sentences.zh: 他人。

sentences.en: And one of his major tips is talk about what the other person is interested in and do it sincerely.
sentences.zh: 他最重要的建议之一就是：谈论对方感兴趣的事，并且要出自真心。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what we're suggesting.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们所建议的。

sentences.en: That when you listen to learn and when you show radical curiosity and an open-hearted mindset, you're paying attention to what the other person says.
sentences.zh: 当你带着学习的心态去倾听，展现出极大的好奇心和敞开心扉的思维模式时，你就是在关注对方所说的话。

sentences.en: And you're doing it in a way that conveys a very strong feeling of, I'm really interested in you and your experience.
sentences.zh: 你这样做的方式传达了一种强烈的感觉：我真的对你和你的经历很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And you would think if you love the other person and you want to be loved back, that this should be easy, right?
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，如果你爱对方，并且希望得到对方的回报，这应该很简单，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you want to do this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你会想这么做。

sentences.en: Oh, I will say that it is not easy.
sentences.zh: 哦，我要说的是，这并不容易。

sentences.en: I would actually say that it's hard.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我要说这很难。

sentences.en: I will tell you, as we were preparing to do this book, Sonia and I attended a workshop in
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你，在我们准备写这本书时，索尼亚和我参加了一个在

sentences.en: Israel on listening, run by Guy Itchikoff, who's one of the world's leading researchers on listening.
sentences.zh: 以色列举办的关于倾听的工作坊，由盖伊·伊奇科夫主持，他是全球顶尖的倾听研究人员之一。

sentences.en: Both of us went into that meeting thinking we were really good listeners.
sentences.zh: 我们俩去参加那个会议时，都觉得自己是非常优秀的倾听者。

sentences.en: We came out of that meeting thinking we got a lot to learn.
sentences.zh: 但从会议出来时，我们觉得自己要学的东西还很多。

sentences.en: It's really hard.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难。

sentences.en: And actually, some of Guy's research shows that a large majority of us feel like we're good listeners.
sentences.zh: 事实上，盖伊的一些研究表明，我们中的绝大多数人都觉得自己是很好的倾听者。

sentences.en: Yet when you ask people how good a listener is that person, the percentages plummet.
sentences.zh: 然而，当你问人们某个人的倾听能力有多好时，百分比就会急剧下降。

sentences.en: The difference is immense.
sentences.zh: 这种差异是巨大的。

sentences.en: And even today, to be honest, there are times when I'm talking to my wife when she says, why don't you do that listening thing you talk about in your book?
sentences.zh: 甚至直到今天，说实话，有时我和妻子交谈时，她会说：“你为什么不做你在书里提到的那种倾听呢？”

sentences.en: Listening is hard because it really requires putting yourself to the side and really trying to immerse yourself in what the other person is saying and doing.
sentences.zh: 倾听很难，因为它确实需要你抛开自我，真正努力沉浸在对方所说和所做的事情中。

sentences.en: And that's something that we're not used to out here in the Western world.
sentences.zh: 而在我们生活的西方世界，这是我们不习惯做的事情。

sentences.en: We've grown up with the idea that the way to move ahead is to show people how good you are, to show people your accomplishments, to individuate yourself compared to other people.
sentences.zh: 伴随着这种观念长大：前进的方法是向人们展示你有多优秀，向人们展示你的成就，在其他人中凸显出你的个性。

sentences.en: And this is suggesting that you do the opposite.
sentences.zh: 而这则建议你做相反的事情。

sentences.en: I know you just mentioned Sonia, Dr. Lubomirsky, who is a well-known happiness researcher, and she was a guest on a previous episode of this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我知道你刚刚提到了索尼亚，柳博姆斯基博士，她是一位知名的幸福感研究员，她曾是本播客上一期的嘉宾。

sentences.en: Why did you decide to write the book together and unite these two areas of research, relationship science and happiness science?
sentences.zh: 你们为什么决定一起写这本书，并将这两个研究领域——关系科学和幸福科学——结合起来？

sentences.en: Oh, there's a wonderful story behind that.
sentences.zh: 哦，这背后有一个美好的故事。

sentences.en: You know, Sonia and I had known each other for a long time because we're in the same field and we would see each other at meetings and such, but we never had worked together.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，索尼亚和我认识很久了，因为我们在同一领域，会在会议之类的地方见面，但我们从未合作过。

sentences.en: And then somewhere around six years ago, we were having a conversation and I naively asked her, what's the number one thing for making a person happy?
sentences.zh: 然后在大约六年前的某个时候，我们在交谈时，我天真地问她：“让人快乐的最重要的事情是什么？”

sentences.en: And without blinking an eye, she said, good social relations.
sentences.zh: 她连眼睛都没眨一下，就说：“良好的社会关系。”

sentences.en: And then she said to me, what's the number one thing that makes for good social relations?
sentences.zh: 然后她反问我：“造就良好社会关系的最重要的事情是什么？”

sentences.en: And I said, you know, feeling loved and connected.
sentences.zh: 我说：“你知道的，就是感到被爱和建立联结。”

sentences.en: And we realized that in both of our disciplines, which are very different areas of research
sentences.zh: 我们意识到，在我们各自的学科中——虽然它们是心理学内部截然不同的研究领域，

sentences.en: within psychology, because we're so siloed as a field, that both of us were actually talking about the same thing.
sentences.zh: 因为我们的学科划分得太细了——但我们俩实际上在讨论同一件事。

sentences.en: And yet we had never come together.
sentences.zh: 然而我们却从未走到一起。

sentences.en: And that's when one of those magical moments happened.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，奇妙的时刻发生了。

sentences.en: We don't actually remember which one of us said we should write a book, but one of us said that.
sentences.zh: 我们其实记不清是我们俩谁先说应该写本书，但总之有人提出来了。

sentences.en: And the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 剩下的就是历史了。

sentences.en: You know, we spent a lot of time sharing ideas from our own individual perspectives, our own literatures.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们花了很多时间分享各自视角、各自文献中的想法。

sentences.en: And gradually they came together in an outline for this book.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，这些想法凝聚成了这本书的写作大纲。

sentences.en: Let me shift gears a little bit and ask what happens when a person is trying to connect with another one and the other person just isn't really responding to these strategies.
sentences.zh: 让我稍微转换一下话题，问一下：当一个人试图与另一个人建立联系，而对方却对这些策略反应冷淡时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: What should you do at that point?
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下你应该怎么做？

sentences.en: Is that a signal that you're basically looking for love in all the wrong places as the song goes?
sentences.zh: 正如那首歌所唱的，这是否是一个信号，表明你基本上是在所有错误的地方寻找爱？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's a great comment, Kim.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的评论，金。

sentences.en: You know, I think one should not expect this to work overnight.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我认为人们不应该指望这能在一夜之间奏效。

sentences.en: If you meet somebody on a first date, let's say, and after three minutes it's not working, I don't think that disqualifies the person.
sentences.zh: 比方说，如果你在第一次约会上遇到某个人，三分钟后行不通，我认为这并不意味着这个人就被否定了。

sentences.en: Sometimes it takes time and sometimes it can happen in a few conversations.
sentences.zh: 有时候这需要时间，有时几次对话就能见效。

sentences.en: Sometimes it can take weeks or months.
sentences.zh: 有时可能需要几周或几个月。

sentences.en: But if you reach the point where it just isn't happening, then it's time to move on.
sentences.zh: 但如果你发现事情毫无进展，那就是时候继续前进了。

sentences.en: And there certainly will be times when that is the case.
sentences.zh: 而且确实会有这种时候。

sentences.en: You know, we don't claim 100% effectiveness.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们不敢保证百分之百有效。

sentences.en: Now, sometimes you'll need to be in a relationship with that person because you work with them or because you see them at family gatherings.
sentences.zh: 有时候，你必须和那个人保持某种关系，因为你们是同事，或者因为你在家庭聚会上会见到他们。

sentences.en: And if that's the case, you know, fine, just accept it and take it for what it is.
sentences.zh: 如果是那样的话，你知道的，好吧，那就接受它，并坦然接受它的本来面目。

sentences.en: But if it's, you know, a more voluntary relationship and not one where you don't necessarily need to continue, well, then, you know, the thing to do is, you know, is to move on.
sentences.zh: 但如果这是一段更加自愿的关系，并不是那种你非得维系不可的关系，那么，你知道的，应该做的事就是继续前进。

sentences.en: There was actually a New Yorker cartoon recently about this idea where it showed a man or woman
sentences.zh: 最近《纽约客》上实际上登过一幅关于这个概念的漫画，里面画着一个男人或女人

sentences.en: talking and the man says, can you please finish talking about yourself quickly so I can spend the next two hours talking about myself?
sentences.zh: 在说话，然后那个男的说：“你能快点讲完你自己的事吗？这样我就可以花接下来两个小时讲我自己的事了。”

sentences.en: And if you're with that kind of a person, then I think the thing to do is to, you know, say thank you very much and move on.
sentences.zh: 如果你和这样的人在一起，那么我认为应该做的就是，你知道的，说声非常感谢然后继续前进。

sentences.en: Now, you just mentioned a moment ago being in relationships with people at work.
sentences.zh: 现在，你刚才提到要处理工作中与他人的关系。

sentences.en: I mean, are we looking for love from the people we work with?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在工作中的人身上寻找爱吗？

sentences.en: Well, in a certain sense, yes.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，是的。

sentences.en: You know, it's certainly not the same as in a romantic relationship.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这当然和浪漫关系不同。

sentences.en: It's certainly not even the same as in a family relationship.
sentences.zh: 甚至也和家庭关系完全不同。

sentences.en: But at the same time, in most work organizations, we're working with other people.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，在大多数工作组织中，我们都在与其他人共事。

sentences.en: And working successfully with other people is an essential component of doing the job in the right way.
sentences.zh: 与他人成功合作是以正确方式完成工作的基本要素。

sentences.en: And we want to feel that we are valued.
sentences.zh: 我们希望感到自己被重视。

sentences.en: We want to feel that other people see our contributions, that they value those contributions, that they're glad to have us as a teammate.
sentences.zh: 我们希望别人看到我们的贡献，重视这些贡献，并庆幸有我们这样的团队成员。

sentences.en: I've been impressed recently with how many professional football players talk about feeling loved by their teammates.
sentences.zh: 最近有很多职业美式橄榄球运动员谈到感受到来自队友的爱，这让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: And that's certainly a setting where you wouldn't expect to see people use that kind of terminology.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一个你不会预料到人们会使用这种术语的环境。

sentences.en: You know, it's different.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是不同的。

sentences.en: It doesn't have, well, obviously it doesn't have the romantic component.
sentences.zh: 它没有——嗯，很明显它没有浪漫的成分。

sentences.en: It may not even have the strong emotional component, but it definitely has the part about being seen and understood and appreciated.
sentences.zh: 它甚至可能没有强烈的感情成分，但它绝对包含被看到、被理解和被欣赏的部分。

sentences.en: And the feeling that other people at work are really concerned about your well-being.
sentences.zh: 并且能感受到工作中的其他人真的在关心你的幸福。

sentences.en: You know, when people at work express condolences when someone in your family passes away, when they celebrate your birthday or some accomplishment of yours at work,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当工作中的人在你家人生病去世时表达哀悼，当他们庆祝你的生日或你在工作中的某项成就时，

sentences.en: that's a way of saying we love you as someone in our group.
sentences.zh: 这就是在说：作为我们团队的一员，我们爱着你。

sentences.en: You know, we're all looking for love somewhere.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们所有人都在某个地方寻找爱。

sentences.en: And there's been a lot of discussion lately about people forming emotional connections with chatbots.
sentences.zh: 最近有很多关于人们与聊天机器人建立情感联系的讨论。

sentences.en: Can you feel something akin to love from a chatbot or an AI companion, or is there something essential that's missing?
sentences.zh: 你能从聊天机器人或人工智能伴侣那里感受到类似于爱的感觉吗，还是说缺少了某种至关重要的东西？

sentences.en: Or are we just deluding ourselves?
sentences.zh: 还是说我们只是在自欺欺人？

sentences.en: That's my favorite question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的问题，金。

sentences.en: Let's say you're starving.
sentences.zh: 假设你饿极了。

sentences.en: You go to the store and you pick up a Snickers bar and you eat it.
sentences.zh: 你去商店拿了一块士力架巧克力并把它吃掉了。

sentences.en: You will stop being hungry for a little while.
sentences.zh: 有一会儿你就不饿了。

sentences.en: It satisfies your hunger.
sentences.zh: 它满足了你的饥饿感。

sentences.en: When people are lonely, when people are not feeling loved, a chatbot can do a great job of filling that need.
sentences.zh: 当人们感到孤独，当人们感到没有被爱时，聊天机器人非常善于满足这种需求。

sentences.en: You know, one of the reasons why chatbots are so effective is that they've been trained on our research.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，聊天机器人如此高效的原因之一是它们接受过我们研究的培训。

sentences.en: They're good at what they do.
sentences.zh: 它们很擅长自己所做的事。

sentences.en: They know how to express appreciation and care and concern for your well-being.
sentences.zh: 它们知道如何表达对你幸福的欣赏、关怀和关注。

sentences.en: They know exactly the right words.
sentences.zh: 它们知道最恰当的词句。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of emerging research that shows that people find the feedback that chatbots give you effective and rewarding.
sentences.zh: 大量新兴研究表明，人们发现聊天机器人提供的反馈既有效又让人有获得感。

sentences.en: So in an immediate sense, those chatbots can be effective.
sentences.zh: 所以在直接的层面上，这些聊天机器人确实有效。

sentences.en: However, let's talk about the long term.
sentences.zh: 然而，让我们谈谈长远来看。

sentences.en: Can they be effective in the long term?
sentences.zh: 从长远来看它们能有效吗？

sentences.en: And the answer, I think, is no.
sentences.zh: 我认为答案是否定的。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that if you just stop and think for a second, you realize that the chatbot doesn't love you.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，如果你停下来思考一秒钟，你就会意识到聊天机器人并不爱你。

sentences.en: The chatbot hasn't made a choice to love you.
sentences.zh: 聊天机器人没有做出爱你的选择。

sentences.en: The chatbot is simply an algorithm spewing out words that it's been programmed to give you.
sentences.zh: 聊天机器人不过是一个算法，吐出它被编程要给你的字词。

sentences.en: Those words feel very good, but when you introspect about those over time, you realize, you know, what is this?
sentences.zh: 这些字词感觉非常好，但随着时间推移，当你对此进行内省时，你会意识到，你知道的，这算什么？

sentences.en: It's a computer program.
sentences.zh: 它只是一个计算机程序。

sentences.en: And so the way we talk about it in our book is the idea that a real loving relationship is like having a nutritious meal.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在书里谈论的方式是这样的概念：一段真正的充满爱的关系就像吃一顿有营养的饭菜。

sentences.en: A relationship with a chatbot is like eating a candy bar.
sentences.zh: 而与聊天机器人的关系就像吃一根糖果棒。

sentences.en: Now, let me contradict myself.
sentences.zh: 现在，我要反驳我刚才说的话。

sentences.en: Let's move 150 years into the future.
sentences.zh: 让我们把时间快进到150年后的未来。

sentences.en: We now have androids that look like human beings, that feel like human beings, that move like human beings,
sentences.zh: 我们现在有了看起来像人类、感觉像人类、移动起来像人类的仿生人，

sentences.en: that are indistinguishable from human beings by any kind of eyeball test, and have AI programmed into their brains.
sentences.zh: 它们在任何目测测试中都与人类无法区分，并且其大脑中编入了人工智能。

sentences.en: In other words, they would pass the Turing test in being indistinguishable from a human being.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它们在与人类无法区分这一点上可以通过图灵测试。

sentences.en: At that point, my answer to your question might well be very different, because at that point,
sentences.zh: 在那个时候，我对你问题的回答可能就会大不相同了，因为到了那个时候，

sentences.en: we might actually be able to live our lives with a non-human version of a human, and at the same time, get all the goodies that we get from close relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上可能能够与人类的非人类版本一起生活，同时获得我们从亲密关系中获得的所有好处。

sentences.en: So I think, you know, my reservations about AI friendships and AI loving relationships are very much applicable to 2026.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，你知道的，我对人工智能友谊和人工智能恋爱关系的保留意见非常适用于2026年。

sentences.en: When that will change, I can't tell you.
sentences.zh: 什么时候会改变，我无法告诉你。

sentences.en: I don't think it will be tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我不认为会是明天。

sentences.en: But I think it's inevitable that we will reach that point at some point in the future.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在未来的某个时候，我们达到那个点是不可避免的。

sentences.en: Well, just to wrap up here, what are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 好了，为了结束今天的访谈，你现在正在做什么？

sentences.en: I mean, what are the questions that you're still trying to answer?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你仍在试图解答哪些问题？

sentences.en: Have you kind of figured out the loving issue, and have you moved on to other things?
sentences.zh: 你算是已经搞清楚爱的议题了吗，还是已经转向了其他事情？

sentences.en: Where are you now?
sentences.zh: 你现在进行到哪一步了？

sentences.en: I'm really focusing my work on the listening component right now, trying to more specifically chart how listening affects people, what the components of good listening are.
sentences.zh: 我目前的工作重点确实放在了倾听组件上，试图更具体地绘制出倾听如何影响人们，以及良好倾听的组成部分是什么。

sentences.en: You know, there are a lot of workshops out there that one can take on listening, and they're very sort of behavioral skill oriented.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，市面上有很多关于倾听的工作坊可以参加，它们非常偏向行为技能导向。

sentences.en: So they'll tell you to make eye contact, to say the person's name three times, to smile four times.
sentences.zh: 所以它们会告诉你进行眼神接触，把对方的名字叫三遍，微笑四次。

sentences.en: And while that can be a start, it's not really what listening is about.
sentences.zh: 虽然这可以算是一个开始，但这并不是倾听的真正意义所在。

sentences.en: What listening is about is connecting with another human being.
sentences.zh: 倾听的意义在于与另一个人类建立连接。

sentences.en: It's really getting into their soul, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 可以这么说，它是真正进入他们的灵魂。

sentences.en: And so what I'd like to do is, you know, more careful work on figuring out exactly how listening works and why it's effective.
sentences.zh: 所以我想做的是，你知道的，做更深入细致的工作，弄清楚倾听到底是如何运作的以及它为什么有效。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Reese, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，里斯博士，我要感谢你今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: This has been very enlightening.
sentences.zh: 这次访谈非常启发人心。

sentences.en: Oh, it's a pleasure to be with you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 哦，很高兴能和你在一起，金。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at speakingofpsychology.org, or on Apple, Spotify, YouTube, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org 上找到《心理学聊斋》（Speaking of Psychology）往期的节目，或者在苹果、Spotify、YouTube 以及任何你获取播客的地方收听。

sentences.en: And if you like what you've heard, please subscribe and leave a review.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢我们讨论的内容，请订阅并留下评价。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future episodes, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的节目有任何意见或想法，你可以给我们发电子邮件，邮箱是 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯，代表美国心理学协会。
